script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. November 3rd, 2026. Can you believe it's already November?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。2026年11月3日。もう11月なんて信じられます？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. Time goes fast. I woke up to rain today.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。時間はあっという間ね。今日は雨で目が覚めたわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, it's pretty dark out there. I really need my coffee today. Looks like it's going to rain all day, doesn't it?
script.ja: ええ、外はかなり暗いですね。今日は本当にコーヒーが必要ですよ。一日中雨が降りそうじゃないですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. The forecast says a 98% chance of rain. Highs around 14.5 degrees, lows around 11.3.
script.ja: そうね。予報では降水確率98%って言ってたわ。最高気温は14.5度くらい、最低気温は11.3度くらいね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ugh, a 98% chance? That's almost certain. Well, at least it's not freezing yet. Still, it feels a bit cold for early November.
script.ja: うわ、98%ですか？ほぼ確実ですね。まあ、まだ凍えるほどじゃないだけマシか。それでも、11月の初めにしてはちょっと寒い気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's definitely sweater weather. Speaking of the news, I saw something about Kumamoto this morning.
script.ja: 完全にセーターの季節ね。ニュースといえば、今朝熊本のことを見たわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, right. I saw a headline. Was it about the earthquake from a while ago?
script.ja: ああ、そうですね。見出しを見ました。少し前の地震のことでしたか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, it was. Three months after the magnitude-7.1 quake, over a thousand people are still in shelters. They're waiting for temporary housing.
script.ja: ええ、そうよ。マグニチュード7.1の地震から3ヶ月経って、まだ1000人以上が避難所で暮らしているって。仮設住宅を待っているのよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: A thousand people? Still? That's... that's really tough. I mean, three months is a long time to be living like that. It's pretty *poignant*, isn't it?
script.ja: 1000人ですか？まだ？それは…それは本当に大変ですね。だって、3ヶ月もそんな生活を送るのは長いですよ。かなり心に迫るものがありますよね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. 'Poignant' means it makes you feel a deep sense of sadness or regret. It touches you emotionally.
script.ja: そうね。「ポイニャント」は、深い悲しみや後悔の念を感じさせる、感情に訴えかけるような、という意味よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, okay. That's a good word for it. My heart goes out to them. I can't imagine trying to raise a baby in a shelter.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。ぴったりの言葉ですね。本当に心が痛みます。避難所で赤ちゃんを育てるなんて、想像もできません。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a very difficult situation. Especially with winter approaching.
script.ja: とても大変な状況よ。特に冬が近づいているからね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. And I also saw something about a construction accident in Aichi. Two workers died. That's just awful.
script.ja: ええ。それから、愛知の建設事故のニュースも見ました。作業員が2人亡くなったって。ひどい話です。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's terrible. Workplace safety is so important, especially in those kinds of environments.
script.ja: 本当にひどいことね。職場の安全はとても大切よ、特にああいう環境では。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It really is. I jump at everything these days, especially loud noises. Pretty sure it's the baby.
script.ja: 全くですね。最近はどんな音にも飛び跳ねてしまいますよ、特に大きな音には。きっと赤ちゃんのせいですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It changes you. My kids are teenagers now, but I still remember. They're both home for the culture festival this weekend.
script.ja: 変わるわよね。私の子供たちはもうティーンエイジャーだけど、まだ覚えているわ。二人とも今週末は文化祭で家にいるの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that's fun! Mine's only a year and five months. It's going to be a while before he's doing culture festivals. Sometimes it feels pretty *daunting* to think about all the things he needs to learn.
script.ja: へえ、楽しそうですね！うちの子はまだ1歳5ヶ月ですからね。文化祭に参加するまでにはまだ時間がかかりますよ。彼が学ぶべきこと全てを考えると、時々かなり気が重くなります。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It just means it feels overwhelming, like a very big challenge. Don't worry, you'll figure it out. One step at a time.
script.ja: それはね、圧倒されるような、とても大きな挑戦だと感じる時に使うのよ。心配ないわ、きっと大丈夫。一歩ずつね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: One step at a time. Right. And speaking of education, did you know that today, November 3rd, is UNESCO Charter Day?
script.ja: 一歩ずつ、ですね。そうですね。教育といえば、今日11月3日はユネスコ憲章記念日だって知ってました？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. The UNESCO Charter was adopted in 1946. Japan joined in 1951.
script.ja: 知ってたわ。ユネスコ憲章は1946年に採択されたの。日本は1951年に加盟したのよね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, its purpose is to promote cooperation between countries through education, science, and culture for world peace and security. That's a big goal.
script.ja: ええ、その目的は、教育、科学、文化を通じて各国間の協力を促進し、世界の平和と安全に貢献することです。大きな目標ですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. And it's still very relevant today.
script.ja: そうね。そして、今日でも非常に重要よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Definitely. It makes you think. Oh, I also saw this funny news story about Japanese college students talking about how anime high school is different from real high school.
script.ja: 間違いなく。考えさせられますね。ああ、そうそう、日本の大学生がアニメの高校と現実の高校がどう違うかについて話している面白いニュース記事も見たんですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Oh? Like what?
script.ja: あら？どんなこと？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Well, they said in anime, you always have these huge, dramatic speeches on the rooftop, right? But in real life, nobody ever goes to the rooftop. It's usually locked.
script.ja: ええと、彼らが言うには、アニメではいつも屋上で壮大で劇的なスピーチがあるでしょう？でも現実では、誰も屋上には行かないって。たいてい鍵がかかってるって。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: That's true. And even if it wasn't, it's not exactly a common place to hang out.
script.ja: それはそうね。それに、たとえ鍵がかかっていなくても、たまり場としては一般的じゃないわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Exactly! They also talked about how anime characters always have super elaborate bento boxes, but real students just eat convenience store food. I thought that was pretty accurate.
script.ja: まさに！あと、アニメのキャラクターはいつもすごく凝ったお弁当を持ってるけど、実際の生徒はコンビニのご飯を食べてるだけだって。それはかなり的を射ていると思いましたね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. It's hard to make those elaborate bentos every day. Especially when you're busy.
script.ja: そうね。毎日あんな凝ったお弁当を作るのは大変よ。特に忙しい時はね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I can barely make my own breakfast these days. This is The Daily Tanu-chan Show, by the way. I almost forgot to say it.
script.ja: ええ、最近は自分の朝食を作るのがやっとですよ。ちなみに、これは「ザ・デイリー・たぬちゃん・ショー」です。言うのを忘れそうになりました。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I know. I'm just finishing my tea before I start work. My garden could use this rain, though. The rosemary is doing well.
script.ja: 知ってるわよ。仕事に取り掛かる前に紅茶を飲み終えるところ。でも、私の庭はこの雨が役に立つわね。ローズマリーはよく育っているわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, that's nice! I always forget you have a garden. Mine is just... potted plants that I sometimes remember to water.
script.ja: ああ、それはいいですね！サラさんが庭を持っていること、いつも忘れちゃいます。僕のはただの鉢植えで、時々水をやるのを思い出す程度ですよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a good way to relax. Well, I should probably get going.
script.ja: 良い気分転換になるわよ。さて、そろそろ行かないとね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Me too. Have a good one, Sarah.
script.ja: 僕もです。良い一日を、サラさん。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You too, Alex. Try not to jump too much today.
script.ja: あなたもね、アレックス。今日はあまり飛び跳ねないようにね。

wikipedia.title: ユネスコ憲章記念日
wikipedia.description: 1946（昭和21）年、ユネスコ（国連教育科学文化機関）が発足。日本は1951（昭和26）年に加盟。ユネスコは、教育・科学・文化を通して各国間の協力を促進し、世界の平和と安全に貢献することが目的。
